rationale: The Latin anchors transcribere, describere, conscribere, and contexere all point firmly to the act of writing/copying or composing a text in writing; the phrase "cuncta per ordinem transcribere curavi" ("I took care to transcribe everything in order") and "quibus scriptura sancta contexta est" ("by which holy scripture is woven/composed") confirm a literary/scribal sense. Among the candidates, write.v.01 ("produce a literary work") best captures this sense of textual composition, as it corresponds to candidate 3's gloss "She composed a poem," which aligns with the OE a-wrītan (literally "to write out/compose in writing").
